excerpt.zh: AX 是 Google 推出的开放式智能体编排控制平面，用沙箱、工作区和网络策略运行大规模、有状态的 AI 任务。
excerpt.en: AX is Google’s open agent orchestration control plane for running large fleets of stateful AI tasks with sandboxes, workspaces, and network policies.

text.zh: AX 如何编排智能体任务
AX 是一个开放式智能体编排控制平面，目标是运行大量有状态、间歇性计算的 AI 任务。用户可以用声明式配置描述任务和工作区，再由 AX 准备代码仓库、工具服务器及运行环境；智能体则在受隔离的沙箱中执行。
text.en: AX is an open agent orchestration control plane aimed at running large numbers of stateful AI tasks with bursty compute patterns. Users describe tasks and workspaces declaratively, while AX prepares repositories, tool servers, and environments before execution. Agents then run inside isolated sandboxes.

text.zh: 它将能力拆成四个核心原语：Task 负责隔离执行，Workspace 负责代码和依赖，Gateway 管理网络访问与凭据，Model 集中管理模型参数和密钥。示例流程支持创建、观察、连接、暂停、恢复和删除任务，保留工作区状态，适合交互式编程、笔记本、浏览器测试以及自定义工具运行时。
text.en: Its design is organized around four primitives: Task for isolated execution, Workspace for code and dependencies, Gateway for network access and credentials, and Model for centralized model settings and secrets. The demonstrated workflow can create, watch, connect to, suspend, resume, and delete tasks while preserving workspace state. This fits interactive coding, notebooks, browser testing, and custom tool runtimes.

text.zh: 面向规模的运行时设计
AX 构建在 Agent Substrate 之上，把每个任务视为轻量级 actor，并尝试通过密集复用工作资源降低等待模型、工具或人工响应时的空闲成本。项目还声称支持亚秒级恢复和每个集群数十亿任务的扩展目标，这些能力服务于大规模轨迹收集、强化学习循环和智能体评估。
text.en: AX is built on Agent Substrate and treats each task as a lightweight actor. It aims to reduce idle cost by multiplexing worker resources while agents wait for model, tool, or human responses. The project also claims sub-second resumption and a target of scaling to billions of tasks per cluster, supporting large-scale trajectory collection, reinforcement-learning loops, and agent evaluation.

text.zh: AX 的关键限制与待验证问题
这些能力目前主要体现为项目方的设计目标和产品说明，来源并未提供独立基准、生产部署数据或成本对比。因此，实际恢复延迟、隔离强度、调度规模、模型调用成本以及长时间运行任务的可靠性，仍需通过公开代码、实验和真实工作负载验证。对于团队而言，声明式体验有吸引力，但运维成熟度与生态兼容性将决定它能否取代现有编排器。
text.en: These capabilities are presented mainly as project goals and product claims; the source provides no independent benchmarks, production deployment data, or cost comparisons. Actual resume latency, isolation strength, scheduling scale, model-call costs, and reliability for long-running tasks still need validation through the public code, experiments, and real workloads. The declarative experience is promising, but operational maturity and ecosystem compatibility will determine whether AX can complement or replace existing orchestrators.
